customer_acme: Hi, we're seeing a bunch of 429s in production since last night. Traffic is a bursty sync job (500 concurrent requests for ~30s), started getting 429s even though project dashboard shows quota available. Can someone help scope where the limit is being applied?

sasha: Sorry about that — can you paste one of the failing request/response headers (no secrets if you want)? 429 body + rate headers are most helpful. Also, are you using a project-scoped API key or an org-level one?

customer_acme: Here's a sanitized example:

Request:
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME_PROJ_abc123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"batch test"}'

Response (truncated):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-scope: org
x-rw-rate-limit-limit: 120000
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 14
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":{"type":"rate_limit_exceeded","scope":"org","retry_after":14}}

We expected project-level scoping; the dashboard shows Project-A has 40k tokens left but org shows exhausted. We also noticed the requests originate from a small set of IPs (we NAT behind a gateway).

maria: Thanks. Two likely possibilities: (1) org-level quota exhausted (billing/commit) and API falls back to org throttle, or (2) there's an IP-based ingress policy that's grouping keys behind your NAT and applying a per-IP burst cap. We'll run checks. In the meantime can you confirm the exact API key header you send (Authorization only, no X-Org-ID)? Also any recent key rotation?

customer_acme: We only send the Authorization header. No X-Org-ID. We did rotate keys yesterday (rotated project key, left org key in place).

eng-ops: Quick triage notes: Redwood enforces multi-tier limits: per-key (project), per-project, per-org, and per-ingress-IP for burst protection. The returned header shows scope=org which means the request was rejected at org quota level. However there are a couple of edge cases that look similar to org 429: auth fallback and billing suspension.

eng-ops: Edge case A (auth fallback): if a project-scoped key is expired/invalid and an org-level backstop key is configured for legacy customers, requests may be authenticated as the org key server-side and hit org quotas. This manifests as a 429 with x-rw-rate-limit-scope: org even if your intent was project-limited.

eng-ops: Edge case B (billing/balance hold): if org billing hits a threshold or invoice fails, system can temporarily switch from per-project metering to org-wide throttling while billing is being processed. That also produces similar headers.

sasha: To help us reproduce, can you run a local burst test and paste the exact curl loop you used? If you can reproduce with a single API key we can confirm whether the throttle is by IP or by key. Example test we run: 

for i in {1..400}; do \
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME_PROJ_abc123" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"prompt":"burst test"}' &\n
done

This will fire ~400 parallel starts. Replace count with smaller number if you want.

customer_acme: Ran that. After ~120 successful requests we start seeing 429s, and the header consistently shows x-rw-rate-limit-scope: org. Logs attached (sanitized):
[2026-02-12T03:12:08Z] request_id=xyz status=200 key=proj-abc tokens=120
[2026-02-12T03:12:08Z] request_id=xyy status=200 key=proj-abc tokens=128
[2026-02-12T03:12:09Z] request_id=xzz status=429 key=org-backstop tokens=0

sasha: That log snippet is telling: one of your requests was authenticated as 'org-backstop'. That aligns with Edge case A (auth fallback). Can you confirm whether you have any client or gateway that may have cached the old org key? Also check whether your rotated project key propagated to all machines.

customer_acme: We do have a CI runner that wasn't updated. Could that explain it?

maria: Yes. If some of your clients are still using the old org key, they will consume org quota. When your burst includes both project-key requests and org-key requests, the org key will get exhausted quicker because it's shared across teams.

support-bot: Automated note: We looked up org usage for acme-corp (org id: org-456). Current org token usage in last 24h: 1.9M tokens of 2.0M committed. Project-A usage: 40k of 100k. Billing status: 1 unpaid invoice (processed; retry in 6h).

sasha: Two concurrent action items: (1) customer: rotate or revoke the old org key on any CI/runner, ensure every node uses the new project key; (2) support/eng: verify billing/invoice fallback doesn't force global throttles prematurely.

eng-ops: For reproducible triage on our side, we'll run a mixed-key burst: 200 requests with proj key + 200 with old org key to see how quota is consumed. We'll also check whether our ingress layer applied an IP burst cap (we throttle per-IP to protect the fleet). If you NAT many clients behind one IP, that cap can kick in even if keys are healthy.

customer_acme: Quick question — can you explain differences between these headers we might see?

eng-ops: Sure, common headers and meanings: 
- x-rw-rate-limit-scope: (org|project|key|ip) — where the rejection occurred
- x-rw-rate-limit-limit: quota window total (tokens or reqs)
- x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: left in window
- x-rw-rate-limit-reset: seconds until window resets
- Retry-After: seconds until you should retry (for 429)

maria: Mitigation options (short-term):
- Revoke stale org keys and ensure all traffic uses project-scoped keys.
- Add client-side token bucket throttling/backoff (exponential) on bursty jobs.
- Request a temporary org burst increase from support if you need one-off heavy backfill.

maria: Long-term: partition workloads across separate projects/keys so a single runaway job doesn't hit shared org quota. Consider Dedicated capacity/Reserved for predictable high-throughput jobs.

billing: FYI — we see an unpaid invoice; if payment fails and billing moves org into grace state, default behavior is to limit new token issuance and route heavy workloads into throttled windows. We'll follow up on payment processing within 6h.

sasha: Next steps: customer to rotate CI runners and re-run the burst test; support to confirm billing status in 4h and eng-ops to run mixed-key reproducer and check ingress IP throttles. If eng-ops confirms an auth fallback bug we'll escalate to runtime team.

customer_acme: Thanks—we rotated keys on all runners and re-tested. After rotation we saw 0 429s for the same bursts. Looks resolved for now. Please keep an eye on billing.

eng-ops: Noted. We'll keep ticket open until billing clears. If anyone else hits mysterious org-level 429s, check: key validity across all clients, whether any backstop org keys exist, NATed IPs hitting ingress caps, and billing grace states.

support-bot: Ticket created: SUP-2026-7890. Assigned to eng-ops and billing.

customer_acme: Appreciate the quick help :clap:
